coaching.headline: Revenant ate our bottom duo alive all game, and we lost nine structures while taking three.
coaching.team: Revenant finished with 13 kills, nine on Kira and Steel, and the most hero damage in the game. The best stretch for the team was a 4-1 teamfight followed by Fangtooth and two enemy outer towers. Both later teamfights went the enemy's way: the first went 2-4, with an inner tower, Orb Prime and two inhibitors falling after that fight, and the second went 1-3 shortly before the Core fell. The enemy turned six of eight won fights into prizes; the team turned two of five.
coaching.lossReflection: The alternative was to make Revenant the fight. Revenant was killable: Iggy & Scorch got Revenant twice, and Kira and Steel once each. Taking teamfights only when Riktor's Skewer, Countess's Feast or Steel's Shield Slam could reach Revenant first, and letting a tower go when none could, aims to shrink the fights Revenant decided. There is no promise the base holds that way, but it beats feeding the same carry all game.

focus.title: Find their carry before trading
focus.action: When their fed carry drops out of sight, Kira and Steel back off toward the nearest teammate and nobody starts a trade until that carry shows again. Next game, count how many of the enemy carry's kills land on our duo.

22.3.call: Steel dropped first to Greystone, yet the team won the fight 4-1 with two Iggy & Scorch kills. Fangtooth and two enemy outer towers followed, but Kira and Steel died in the skirmish between the tower takes. Take the prize, then reset.

25.5.call: Iggy & Scorch fell first to Greystone; Countess killed Belica and Greystone while Revenant killed Kira, Riktor and Steel. An inner tower fell during it and Orb Prime soon after. Two kills mean nothing while their best damage still stands.

30.6.call: The team took an enemy outer tower in this window, but Steel, Kira and Riktor died for one kill on Aurora, and the Core fell shortly after. With two inhibitors already lost, staying alive to defend outranks any tower.

80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.matchup: The jungle opponent was Aurora: magical damage, the Glacial Charge dash that leaves a wall, the Hoarfrost ring that roots and Cryoseism, which slows and then stuns. Aurora finished with the most objective damage in the game and killed Riktor twice. Belica killed Riktor three times with a basic-attack build, and Revenant, the physical crit carry, had the most kills in the game.
80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.build: Spectral Schematics adds damage when Riktor immobilizes a target, with Skewer's suppress as the main tool for it. Flux Matrix brings magical armor against Aurora and makes nearby enemy heroes take more magical damage with less tenacity, which suits Riktor's magical abilities and a team dealing mostly magical damage. Elafrost and Tainted Guard add physical armor; Tainted Guard also cuts healing and bleeds anyone who basic-attacks Riktor, relevant against Revenant and Belica.
80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.eternal: Knell applies Rust on hero hits, shredding both armors and giving Riktor part of what it removes. Patina adds a shield and movement speed after a stretch without taking damage, and Fracture adds damage against targets at maximum Rust. Both the shred and the armor share depend on repeated hits on the same hero. Resonant Repair, which heals and adds tenacity whenever Riktor is immobilized, is the draft alternative to Fracture against Aurora's root and stun, Belica's stun and Revenant's root, trading damage for surviving lockdown.
80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.augment: Wanton Warden regenerates health equal to part of the damage taken, growing with level. It suits a jungler who took more damage than anyone in the game, but it is recovery after the hit, not protection from burst. Brutal Chains is the alternative if landing Riplash more often matters more: a longer pull whose cooldown drops on a hit, giving up the sustain.
80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.crest: Saphir's Mantle grows Riktor's size and maximum health for a few seconds, damages nearby heroes, then permanently adds health based on the damage dealt. It rewards walking into the fight and staying on heroes while it is active, which matches a frontline jungler. Activations are not recorded, so whether it was available for any given fight is unknown.
80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21.improvement: The winning core is Elafrost, Spectral Schematics and Gaia Greaves; Riktor ran the first two and took Flux Matrix and Tainted Guard instead of Gaia Greaves. Tainted Guard already covers physical armor and adds anti-heal against basic attackers, and Flux Matrix answers Aurora's magic, so the build is a sound keep. Gaia Greaves trades that anti-heal for movement-based damage that drains while Riktor is slowed or immobilized. Nothing in this match proves a build change.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: The lane opponent was Lt. Belica, built on basic attacks, with Seismic Assault's stun and Neural Disruptor's silence. Iggy & Scorch killed Belica four times and never died to Belica. The real threats were physical: Greystone, who closes distance with the Assault The Gates leap and killed Iggy & Scorch twice, and Revenant, with the most hero damage in the game.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Every slot is magical power with health and no armor. Megacosm adds damage based on maximum and bonus health, Magnify strips magical armor on ability hits, Dreambinder slows on ability damage at a reduced rate for damage over time, Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage and World Breaker stacks magical damage while adding tenacity. Those effects suit a kit built on fire zones and turrets. Greystone's Tainted Bastion adds magical armor and cuts the healing of whoever hits Greystone with magic.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Aion gives mana regeneration on spell casts and gold from spell damage to heroes; Philosopher generates gold over time and Arcane Resonance speeds basic ability cooldowns and Philosopher with mana regeneration. That is an economy setup, and Iggy & Scorch finished with the most gold in the game, though the record cannot split how much came from it. Perfection, which adds ability haste while near full health, is the draft alternative to Arcane Resonance.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: Hold This! makes Molotov's explosion permanently stronger against heroes each time it hits one, so it rewards landing Molotov on heroes all game. Hit counts are not recorded. Badlands Belch is the alternative if finishing low targets matters more: Inferno's Belch gains missing-health damage and a farther knockback, giving up the stacking Molotov damage.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Epoch puts Iggy & Scorch into stasis for a short stretch. It adds no distance, so it pays when teammates can turn on a diver during it, which fits Greystone's leap or Revenant's commit. Activations are not recorded, so whether it was available in the deaths to Greystone and Revenant is unknown.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: Greystone and Revenant, both physical damage dealers, accounted for all three deaths, and nothing in the build adds armor. With three deaths and the most gold in the game, the damage build is a sound keep. If physical divers start ending fights before the fire zones go down, a physical armor item in place of one damage item is the comparison, trading damage for surviving the first engage.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: The lane opponent was Greystone: physical damage, the Assault The Gates leap, a passive that deflects a basic attack on a cooldown and gains physical armor and regeneration as health drops, and Stone Forged Soul's stasis heal. Countess killed Greystone twice and never died to Greystone. Tainted Bastion gave Greystone magical armor and cuts the healing of whoever hits Greystone with magic, which touches Blade Siphon and Feast healing.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Noxia marks heroes hit by ability damage and adds maximum-health damage when a different ability hits the mark, which suits Countess's ability chains. Overseer makes Feast hit harder and heal from the damage. Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage, relevant against Narbash, who had the most healing in the game, and Greystone's regeneration. Orb Of Enlightenment adds health and heals on ability casts. Nothing here adds armor of either type.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Vesh turns part of Countess's ability damage to heroes into damage over time, Lich adds magical lifesteal by level and Mind Rot adds current-health damage to the Vesh effect. It fits a spell-damage Countess. Greystone's Tainted Bastion, Narbash's Tainted Totem and Belica's Tainted Rounds all cut healing, so Tithe of Death is the draft alternative to Lich: takedowns restore mana and add permanent ability haste, giving up lifesteal this lobby could reduce.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Sanguine Slash makes Blade Siphon deal more damage and heal more against isolated targets. It pays when Countess catches a lone target and adds nothing extra in a crowded fight; the record cannot show how often isolated targets were available. Shadow Strike is the alternative if Shadow Slip uptime matters more, trading the isolated-target bonus for faster repositioning.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Tempest damages up to three nearby heroes every second during its active window and heals for part of it. With Blade Siphon also hitting everything around Countess, it suits staying inside a fight. Activations are not recorded.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: The matchup flag notes no armor against a three-physical enemy lineup. Countess died only twice, once to Aurora's magic and once to Revenant, so armor is not proven necessary here. If Revenant or Greystone start ending fights before Feast lands, physical armor in place of a damage item is the comparison, trading burst for surviving the first exchange. As built, it is a sound keep.

d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.matchup: Duo was Kira and Steel against Revenant and Narbash. Revenant is a physical crit carry: Scar roots once its marks are consumed, and Reckoning slows the target and pulls it into the Nether Realm with Revenant while stealing some of its power. Narbash heals, stuns with Thunk and mesmerizes with Crash Bang Boom. Revenant killed Kira four times and Aurora, with a root and a stun, killed Kira three times.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.build: Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or attacking and slows with the empowered shot. Tainted Rounds cuts healing on basic attacks, the right answer to Narbash's healing and Revenant's lifesteal. Imperator raises critical damage. Onixian Quiver fires extra projectiles on ranged basic attacks, but its Onixia passive, extra crit chance and mitigation, works only for melee heroes, so Kira gets the stats and projectiles without that bonus. Nothing in the build adds defense.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.eternal: Vermis adds maximum-health physical damage on every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero, Serration adds missing-health damage to it, and Breach makes ultimate damage cut physical armor briefly, so Purge sets up the follow-up shots. It rewards long, uninterrupted shooting on one target. Sub-Surface, which reduces damage from area abilities, is the draft alternative to Breach if surviving brawls matters more than the armor cut.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.augment: Bringer Of Mercy makes Mercy cheaper and shortens Kira's current cooldowns whenever Mercy deals damage, which cycles Shadow Glide and Dusk faster in long fights. Siphoning Purge is the alternative if Kira needs sustain: Purge heals for part of its hero damage, giving up the cooldown cycling.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.crest: Pacifier dashes, empowers the next physical damage instance and allows a recast after a hero kill. Kira's damage is physical, so the empowered hit applies, and the dash stacks another escape on Shadow Glide and Blink. Activations are not recorded, so whether it was available in the deaths to Revenant and Aurora is unknown.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab.improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator; Kira kept Imperator and went basic-attack heavy instead. The clearer adjustment is defense: Revenant and Aurora accounted for seven of Kira's eight deaths and nothing in the build protects Kira. If Revenant keeps winning the meetings, a defensive item in place of Onixian Quiver is the comparison, since its Onixia passive does nothing for a ranged hero, trading attack speed and extra projectiles for surviving the burst.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Duo was Steel and Kira against Revenant and Narbash. Revenant killed Steel five times with physical crit damage, and Narbash, with the most healing in the game, adds the Thunk stun and the Crash Bang Boom mesmerize. Aurora's root and stun and Greystone's leap were the other threats, each killing Steel twice.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Warden's Faith is the direct answer to Revenant: Steel takes less critical-strike damage and nearby enemies lose some physical power. Dynamo makes immobilized enemies take more damage, which Steel's stuns trigger. Xenia adds both armors and shields allies close to Steel, so it only helps Kira when the duo stays together. There is no anti-heal here, though the team carried four anti-heal items.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size, Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after a stretch without hero damage and Cannibalism adds permanent health on takedowns. It is a plain health stack for a tank support. Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue: Steel's stuns would cut healing on the target, including a lifestealing Revenant, giving up the out-of-combat regeneration.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Heavy Metal adds magical on-hit damage to heavy punches and Shield Bash based on total physical and magical armor, so every armor item in this build feeds it. Bulldozer is the peel-minded alternative: Bull Rush gains damage reduction while Steel is unstoppable, giving up the armor-based damage.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Sanctification shields Steel and nearby heroes for a few seconds with extra tenacity while the shield holds, raises the ward cap and reduces minion gold. Against Narbash's stun and mesmerize and Revenant's root, the tenacity has a clear purpose. Activations are not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: The winning core is Fire Blossom, Raiment of Renewal and Tainted Charm; Steel built none of them. Warden's Faith is the piece to keep against a crit carry like Revenant. Tainted Charm cuts healing and slows enemies just by standing near them, the swap if Revenant's lifesteal or Narbash's healing starts winning fights, at the cost of Xenia's ally shields. With four anti-heal items already on the team, the current build is a sound keep.

80061dae-e995-49c2-8f5e-a7f43c450d21: Riktor ate more damage than anyone in the game and had a hand in more of our kills than anyone else on the team. That is a frontline jungler doing the dirty work.
Nine deaths is too many naps for a jungler, and three came before the ten-minute mark, two of them in their half of the map. Early on, Riktor enters their jungle only when Iggy & Scorch can follow.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 had the strongest game on our side: the most gold in the game, our top hero and objective damage, four kills on Belica and two on Revenant, three deaths. Keep that shit exactly as it is.

Greystone got two of those three deaths, including the first death in the lost teamfight before Orb Prime. Save Epoch for the Assault The Gates leap so Countess and Riktor have time to turn on Greystone.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster kept the offlane clean: the fewest deaths on our team, farm well above the Countess baseline, two kills on Greystone without dying to Greystone, and tied for the most wards placed in the game.
Countess had a hand in only five of our kills, the fewest on the team. When Aurora or Revenant commits onto Kira or Iggy & Scorch, ping and bring Feast to that fight.
d8e939b6-c450-43c9-873f-cb09940aacab: KingRatt45 put out carry damage, a hair behind Iggy & Scorch for our best, but farmed well under the Kira baseline. Seven kills and eight deaths is a coin flip, not a fucking carry game.

Two Kira deaths came outside any detected fight, one shortly before their first Fangtooth and one shortly before Orb Prime. With a major about to spawn, Kira farms within reach of the group and walks in with the team.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs had a hand in just over half our kills, the second-most damage mitigated in the game and the only ward anyone cleared, but placed fewer wards than Narbash.
Revenant killed Steel five times and Kira four, treating the duo like an open buffet. Next game, Bull Rush has one job: stop that crit merchant the moment Revenant steps toward Kira.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Narbash. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 4 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback), Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Riktor, Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 magical — predictable; one magic-resist item answers most of it. Mix in a physical threat.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
ourKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
ourKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
ourKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

ourKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
ourKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

ourKits.combo: Shadow Slip in → Eventide → Blade Siphon → Feast suppress ult, Haemorrhage true-damage
ourKits.winCondition: Feast-suppress a squishy and delete them with true-damage burst
ourKits.passive: two-ability hits apply a %max-HP true-damage bleed
ourKits.playWith: a team to clean up after her pick
ourKits.playAgainst: Feast is her whole engage — bait it / peel; she's fragile, punish the recast window

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
enemyKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

enemyKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
enemyKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

enemyKits.combo: Thunk stun → March! speed → Song heal aura → Crash Bang Boom! AoE slow ult
enemyKits.winCondition: engage with Thunk and group-buff the team through fights
enemyKits.playWith: a dive team that rides his speed and heal
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge/cleanse Thunk; he's low-damage — kill his carry through the aura
